**Collage** turns a folder of photos into a print-ready poster: one picture per slot on a calendar-style grid.

It is good for family timelines, project archives, “one photo per month” walls — anything where the story is a grid over time.

![Example collage poster](assets/example.jpg){fig-alt="Example monthly photo collage poster" width=70%}

<p class="caption-note">Example output — your photos, your crops, same idea.</p>

## What you get

- A **Shiny app** (`app.R`) to assign photos to slots, crop them to squares, and generate a poster into `output/`
- Optional **`poster.qmd`** to fine-tune DPI, gaps, and labels without opening the app
- Safe **demo tiles** under `images/demos/` so a fresh copy works before you add real photos

## Default grid

The starter layout is **12 months × 19 years** (slots `0801` … `2612` — January 2008 through December 2026), laid out as a **12-column × 19-row** poster on A1 paper.

You can change that in the app’s **Setup** tab (danger zone): rows, columns, gap, paper size, and how slots are named (year–month calendar, row×column ids, or simple `1…n`). Reshape **resets** slot data and can recreate demos for the new cells.

> After editing this file, re-render with Quarto (`quarto render index.qmd`) to refresh `index.html`, or edit `index.html` directly if Quarto is not installed.

## Quick start

1. Install R packages: `shiny`, `magick`, `base64enc`
2. Open this folder in R / RStudio
3. If demos are missing: `source("assets/setup.R"); setup_collage(demo = TRUE)`
4. Run the app: `shiny::runApp(".")`
5. Put photos in `images/import/` (or pick files in **Edit slot**), crop, then **Generate poster**

Full walkthrough: see [README.md](README.md).

## Two ways to make the poster

| In the app | Fine-tune separately |
|------------|----------------------|
| **Poster** tab → Generate poster → `output/poster.jpg` | Prep images in the app, then render `poster.qmd` for print control |
